elements.scope_reason: Red box: urgent attention for suicidal thoughts or behaviour.
elements.problem: Both parts (suicidal thoughts; suicidal behaviour) are checked for and the Urgent priority rule is structured as (and <presenting complaint> (or <red-box items>)) per the house standard. Both SNOMED concepts exist as named. Note only: in SNOMED 'Suicidal behavior' is a descendant of 'Suicidal thoughts', so the (or ...) is redundant in due_to (descendants match automatically) but not wrong, and listing both in check_for is reasonable for the nurse-facing checklist. The page's '-> 34' is a cross-reference and is out of scope.
evidence: Check for urgent low mood, stress or anxiety conditions :: (check_for (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Suicidal thoughts" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Suicidal behavior" "finding")))

Urgent: low mood, stress or anxiety with suicidal thoughts or behaviour :: (and (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Depressed mood" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Stress" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Anxiety" "finding"))) (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Suicidal thoughts" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Suicidal behavior" "finding"))))

elements.problem: 'If patient known with depression, give routine depression care instead -> 160' is routing to another page; the language has no way to express 'use another page instead'. The trigger (Depressed mood / Stress / Anxiety) is the builders' choice of presenting complaint and matches the page title.

elements.scope_reason: The Anxiety row carries the page's diagnostic logic: two 'X likely' conclusions (GAD, PTSD) and one named-condition bullet (phobia / panic).
parts_missing: Bullet 1 (GAD likely): 'causes impaired function/distress' is encoded as Distress only; the 'impaired function' alternative is not encoded, so the probable GAD rule requires Distress and will not fire for a patient whose excessive worry impairs function without reported distress. (No SNOMED concept for generic impaired function was found by search; the rule should at least note this or use the and-with-Distress as a documented approximation.)

Bullet 2 (phobia / panic): nothing is encoded. The page names two conditions ('induced by a particular situation/object (phobia)', 'repeated sudden fear with physical symptoms and no obvious cause (panic)') and the house standard treats a named condition the page wants recognised as at least a possible diagnosis or a check_for item. SNOMED has (snomed_concept "Phobia" "finding"), (snomed_concept "Panic attack" "finding") and (snomed_concept "Panic disorder" "disorder"). The 'discuss/refer' action itself is a management step and out of scope.
elements.problem: Part-by-part: (1) GAD likely: PARTIAL. Duration '(>= (onset Worried+Excessive) (time_ago 6 months))' correctly means onset at least 6 months ago; 'excessive worry' as Worried with qualifier Excessive is a fair encoding; the '>= 3 of 6' is enumerated exactly (A+any2(rest) | B+any2(rest) | C+any2(rest) | D+E+F covers every 3-subset of {muscle tension, restlessness, irritability, difficulty sleeping, poor concentration, tiredness}); the six symptom concepts map correctly (tiredness -> Fatigue, irritability -> Feeling irritable). Only the impaired-function alternative is missing. (2) Phobia/panic: MISSING (see parts_missing). (3) PTSD likely: CORRECT. '> 1 month' is encoded as (>= (onset Anxiety) (time_ago 1 months)), which is 'at least 1 month' rather than strictly more; immaterial. 'linked to a bad experience' -> Victim of psychological trauma is a reasonable concept (parent: Victim of trauma). The four groups (nightmares/flashbacks; avoids situations/people; on guard/easily startled; numb/detached from others/surroundings) are each an (or ...) so a group counts once, and '>= 3 of 4' is enumerated exactly as (G1 and any2(G2,G3,G4)) or (G2 and G3 and G4). 'feels numb/detached from others/surroundings' -> Emotionally detached + Derealization is a fair split. All concepts exist as named. The '-> 160' and 'discuss/refer' are out of scope.

elements.scope_reason: A two-question depression screen with a time window ('in the past month') whose only consequence is a cross-reference (-> 159). The criteria are expressible (Depressed mood, Feeling hopeless, Loss of interest / Anhedonia exist in SNOMED) and the house standard's check_for lists are meant to mirror what the page tells the nurse to ask; but the page reaches no 'X likely' here, so treating it as cross_reference_only is defensible.
parts_missing: felt down/depressed/hopeless in the past month
little interest/pleasure in doing things in the past month
elements.problem: Neither screening question is in a check_for and no rule consumes them. Depressed mood appears only as one of the page's trigger findings, not as something the page asks the nurse to elicit. If encoded, a check_for of (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Feeling hopeless" "finding")) and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Loss of interest" "finding")) with a possible-depression rule, or nothing at all, are both acceptable readings; the file documents neither.

elements.scope_reason: A substance-use screen with explicit thresholds ('in the past year', '>= 4 drinks/session', illegal drugs, misused prescription/OTC medication) whose only consequence is a cross-reference (-> 165). Same reasoning as the depression row.
parts_missing: >= 4 drinks per session in the past year
illegal drug use in the past year
misuse of prescription or over-the-counter medication in the past year
elements.problem: Nothing encoded. The drinks-per-session threshold has no unit in the language, so that part is arguably not_representable; the drug-use and medication-misuse parts could be plain findings. Low consequence: the page routes to page 165 rather than concluding anything here.
'If patient is being abused -> 33' has no criterion beyond the cross-reference.

Stressors row: 'help identify psychosocial stressors', 'ask about loneliness', 'refer to social club' are management/assessment prompts; 'if sexual problems -> 74' and 'life-limiting illness / in bed or chair >= 50% of day / dependent -> also give palliative care 191' are cross-references to other pages. None leads to a diagnosis or priority on this page.

Women's health row: 'recent delivery -> postnatal care 182', 'woman > 40 years, ask about menopausal symptoms ... -> 74' are management prompts and cross-references, not diagnostic logic for this page.

Medication row: 'review medication ... can cause mood changes. Discuss with doctor. Consider alternative contraceptive -> 187' is a management step. A reviewer could argue that a check_for of current prednisone/efavirenz/metoclopramide/theophylline/contraceptive use is useful, but the house standard does not require it and no diagnosis is reached.
'Review every 2-4 weeks. If no improvement after 3 months, assess for depression/anxiety -> 159' is follow-up scheduling plus a cross-reference.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable generalised anxiety disorder (low mood, stress or anxiety page)
rule_level_problems.problem: The page's condition is 'excessive worry causes impaired function/distress'; the rule ANDs Distress unconditionally, dropping the impaired-function alternative. The rule is therefore stricter than the page: a patient with 6+ months of excessive worry, functional impairment and >= 3 symptoms but no recorded Distress gets no GAD diagnosis. If no SNOMED concept for functional impairment can be found, the approximation should be documented; otherwise add it as an (or Distress <impairment>) alternative.

The page's second Anxiety bullet names phobia and panic as recognisable patterns ('induced by a particular situation/object (phobia)'; 'repeated sudden fear with physical symptoms and no obvious cause (panic)') and nothing in the file captures either: no check_for item, no possible diagnosis. (snomed_concept "Phobia" "finding") and (snomed_concept "Panic attack" "finding") exist. A possible rule or at least check_for items would match the house standard's 'consider X' treatment; the discuss/refer action itself is out of scope.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for generalised anxiety disorder and PTSD features / Diagnose probable generalised anxiety disorder
rule_level_problems.problem: The qualified finding (Worried + Excessive) appears in the probable rule only as the subject of (onset ...), never as a bare clinical_finding in due_to. Will's constraints match evidence by exact s-expression string; if the test does not look inside onset(), the check_for item will be reported as 'checked for but never used' and the rule's onset evidence as 'not checked for'. The briefing cites page 48 as a working precedent for onset in due_to, so this is probably fine; flagging so the database test run confirms it.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for urgent low mood, stress or anxiety conditions / Check for generalised anxiety disorder and PTSD features / Urgent: ...
rule_level_problems.problem: All three rules trigger on (or Depressed mood / Stress / Anxiety). None of these is a listed common symptom or warning sign in the briefing, so the page's rules only fire if some other page or intake records one of these findings. Acceptable per the briefing ('most natural clinical_finding for the complaint'), but it should be in the remaining-questions file and the SNOMED 'Stress' finding (a mood finding) should be confirmed as the intended recorded form rather than 'Stress' qualifier value.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: low mood, stress or anxiety with suicidal thoughts or behaviour
rule_level_problems.problem: Not a defect, for the record: 'Suicidal behavior' is a SNOMED descendant of 'Suicidal thoughts', so (or Suicidal thoughts Suicidal behavior) collapses to Suicidal thoughts in due_to. Harmless redundancy; keeping both in check_for is reasonable for the nurse-facing list.

summary: The red box and the two 'X likely' conclusions (GAD, PTSD) are encoded with correct concepts, correct duration semantics and exact enumerations of '>= 3 of N'. The most consequential gap is in the GAD rule, which requires Distress and drops the page's 'impaired function' alternative, making it stricter than the page. The phobia/panic bullet is not encoded at all (no check_for, no possible rule), and the depression and substance-use screening questions are left unencoded, which is defensible as cross-reference routing but undocumented.
